source_caption:
To capture the wildly terrifying, deeply unpredictable tension of the film’s most iconic standoff, director Alex Garland originally cast another actor to play the fiercely chilling, violently xenophobic militia soldier. However, when that actor abruptly dropped out just days before filming, star Kirsten Dunst completely saved the production by simply suggesting her real-life husband, Jesse Plemons, who happened to be nearby and available. Stepping into the heavily intense role at the very last minute, Plemons brought a deeply unsettling, eerily calm cadence to the performance, turning the incredibly simple question—“What kind of American are you?”—into the most profoundly unforgettable moment of the entire movie. By trusting a massive, last-minute pivot to a brilliantly unhinged character actor, Garland masterfully proves that the most viscerally terrifying cinematic encounters often happen entirely by accident.
⠀
Civil War (2024), directed by Alex Garland, starring Kirsten Dunst, Wagner Moura, Cailee Spaeny. In a fiercely fractured, rapidly collapsing United States, a deeply exhausted, highly seasoned team of military embedded journalists desperately races across a wildly dangerous, heavily combat-torn dystopian landscape to reach Washington D.C. before rebel factions completely overthrow the intensely besieged federal government.

source_details.synopsis: Civil War is a 2024 dystopian war-thriller film written and directed by Alex Garland, and starring Kirsten Dunst, Wagner Moura, Cailee Spaeny, Stephen McKinley Henderson, Sonoya Mizuno, and Nick Offerman. Set during a second American civil war fought between a despotic federal government and secessionist movements, the plot follows a group of war journalists traveling from New York City to Washington, D.C., to interview the president of the United States before rebels take the capital city. Principal photography began in Atlanta, Georgia, in 2022, with production moving to London later in the year.
